notes.title: Version 1.1 is now available!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38454270/40cf273aac7d4cbcdab581fcaba49bebbcc33480.png[/img]

The new update for 86 is available now! This is our biggest update yet, bringing a few new big features as well as a few smaller improvements. We discussed the big changes back in our November update, but here's a recap as well as a list of the other changes in this update!

[h2]Sprinting[/h2]
Sluggle can now sprint! Holding the Sprint button (Left Shift on keyboard, Y on Xbox controller by default) allows you to move at double the speed, which will help you get across large areas where precision isn't needed, and give you more time to solve the more intricate puzzles further away from the starting area. But if you're going for the speedrun achievements, you'll still have to complete the winning run without sprinting at all!

[h2]Statistics Screen[/h2]
You can now find the Statistics button hanging out on the main menu. Hit it to look at how many Sluggles you've led to their deaths, or (a much smaller number) their victory. You can also see your best times with and without sprinting, and how many rooms you've explored in total. It will even show your progress towards the hidden achievements... technically.

[h2]Small improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*]Updated puzzles on one of the optional paths to make it impossible to cheese by sprinting
[*]Made the Hide button faded when it doesn't do anything (e.g. immediately after loading the game, before starting any runs)
[*]Added colour to some rocks to make the similar ones stand out more from each other
[*]Shrunk the Loony Code logo on the loading screen
[*]Made the triggers for the hidden achievements a bit more generous
[*]Added a faint flickering border to give the it that "old monitor" feel
	- This can be turned off by disabling "Border Animation" in the options
[*]Updated the UI scale setting so that you can't make the interface unplayably huge for your screen
[*]Changed the texture for tabs in the options menu, so that it's easier to see which tab is selected
[/list]

[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Changed some tiles that didn't connect properly to others
[*]Fixed some optional rooms to remove unintended and boring solutions
[*]Changed the font in the options slightly to fix some text not fitting on the buttons
[*]Fixed another room that had a random grass tile in some water
[/list]

If you've made a custom translation, there are also a few new phrases that can be added; check the Text.mbt file in the game folder to see what's new.

That's all for now - be sure to let us know if you find any bugs, and get in touch if there's any features you want to see in future updates!

notes.title: Development update for 1.1
notes.notes:
Hello Sluggle buddies,

It's been a few weeks since the last update to 86, so we thought we would let you know what we're working on. Lots of our time has been spent on our larger project, but we've also been working on 86 in preparation for the upcoming 1.1 update. In this post we'll go through a couple of the major features you'll be seeing soon.

As a recap, the features we've added since release include:
[list]
[*] A "getting started" guide
[*] Support for community translations
[*] Faded borders
[*] Various improvements to level design
[/list]
And now, onto two of the main features coming in the 1.1 update:


[h2]Sprinting[/h2]

This is a feature that we didn't originally envision, but we think we've found a way to make it work. In 1.1, there will be a new "sprint" button (defaults to Left Shift on keyboard and Y on controller, but can be configured in the options). Holding this button down will allow you to zip across the world at double speed, allowing you to cross large areas much faster than usual.

Of course, with great power comes great responsibility. If you try to sprint everywhere, you'll find that it's almost impossible to make the precise movements that lots of the puzzles require. But used correctly, it will save you a few seconds here and there, making it easier to get to some of the farthest rooms.

For the most part, there is no penalty for sprinting and most achievements will still unlock. The only exception are the speedrun achievements; your fastest wins with sprinting and without sprinting will be tracked separately, and the achievements will check the "without sprinting" time.

Speaking of which...


[h2]Statistics[/h2]

Currently, the game tracks various statistics such as number of deaths, rooms explored, and fastest win times. This is used to trigger achievements, but it's not available anywhere for you to see. So in this update, we'll add a dedicated statistics screen to the main menu! Here's a very rough drawing that shows how we expect it to look:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38454270/81c687bfcc96a34cbddca7715c55bd2275ebb7a1.png[/img]
[i](Yes, it was our Software Director that drew that, not the Art Director. How did you know?)[/i]

As you can see, this screen will show you pretty much all the data that's stored in your save file. So whether you want to see how fast you can beat the game or just want to know how many poor Sluggles you've exploded, we've got your back.


[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

So that's a couple of the features we're working on at the moment, which will be coming in the 1.1 update. There's at least one other feature that we'll be adding, but that's still in the RnD phase at the moment. Currently we don't have an exact time frame for the update, but it should definitely be out before the end of the year.

That's all for now - if there's anything else you want to see in the 1.1 update, let us know with a comment below!

notes.title: Version 1.0.2 is available!
notes.notes:
This version brings a couple of small but much-needed improvements:

[h2]Adding some clutter[/h2]
There were a couple of rooms that had puzzles that looked fairly simple, but were intended to be solved after more exploration and rule-learning. To stop brave souls from trying to solve them without the required knowledge, we've added a bit more to those rooms (without altering the overall solution), so that we don't accidentally trick anyone into trying to solve a puzzle that's harder than it looks.

[h2]Faded edges[/h2]
We've cleaned up the edges of the screen a bit, so you'll now see a fade effect along the walls of each room. This will make things look a bit less weird when you get to the edge of a room and, let's face it, it adds to the atmosphere!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38454270/08ee218b3381dc013d9e5b47636c834bd7be7645.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38454270/1c486cb70097dbb5ad2993888c9042607fac8775.png[/img]


That's all for this update; we've got some more ideas that we'd like to add further down the line. But those are a bit bigger than things we've done so far, so watch this space. As always, feel free to jump into the discussions if you want to chat, report any issues or make any suggestions!

notes.title: Version 1.0.1 is available! Plus "Getting Started" guide
notes.notes:
It's been 2 weeks since 86 was released, and today we're happy to release our first minor update! Version 1.0.1 brings a few bug fixes, as well as support for some basic community translations.

[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Removed a stray grass tile in the water in one of the northernmost rooms
[*] Fixed a bug where applying the options would cause the Apply button to not show as selected, even though it actually was
[*] Some minor cleanup of the code that will have no effect on the game but will hopefully stop me breaking more stuff in the future
[/list]


[h2]Community translation[/h2]

This version also adds support for community translations, allowing you to use your own text (or someone else's) ingame instead of the default, plain English text. This is currently an experimental feature with a lot of limitations, but if you're interested in seeing it developed further, let us know!
To learn more, see the guide [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2231518834]here[/url].


[h2]Getting Started guide[/h2]

Finally, we've noticed that some players have had trouble working out how to start - after all, it's an unusual world and there's so many directions to explore! We've also uploaded a guide that will show you how to solve a few of the game's initial puzzles, to teach you how to begin solving puzzles and exploring the world without giving too much away. If you've picked up the game but haven't got past the first few rooms, check the guide [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2231488772]here[/url] for an overview of what to do next.

Happy exploring!
